notes:
aurora_lint 1504 (v0.5.3 step 3), MSC01-C batch 3 of 3: valkey baseline. valkey had no MSC01-C labels. Held until aurora_lint 1535 (EXP19-C/MSC01-C comment-as-body and spliced-chain fix, d2453457) landed, then released by the coordinator. Stacked on the previous 1504 branch off benchmark_adjudication main 157bd9b; this branch adds only this batch's rows over its parent.

POPULATION. Postgres realworld run 274 (aurora-lint 05bd14f9) unlabeled in-scope valkey MSC01-C keys (401), diffed against main. A local probe at d2453457 (MSC01-C + EXP19-C only, via bench.realworld_runner._build_sqc_cmd, corpus-check clean; a diagnostic, not a project figure) shows 1535 removes none of them, so all 401 are labeled; split by file into three batches.

STANDARD. The existing MSC01-C convention (~2,400 labels, ~95% FP): FP when the missing final else or default is the intentional no-op or fall-through of a guard-clause, error-check or optional-behaviour idiom, when values are handled by code after the chain, or when the chain covers every possible value; TP when a dispatch over an enumeration, state or mode set leaves legitimate values silently unhandled with no fallback. A switch or chain over a bitfield or mask wider than its declared enumerators, with no default and no fallback, is TP at medium, matching the sel4 notification/endpoint/vspace labels. Config-gated arms count as written (ADR-0010).

METHOD. One read-only agent per batch, briefed with the convention above, with every TP and flagged call spot-checked at source by the adjudicator.

RESULT: 132 FP / 4 TP. With batches 1-2 this covers every in-scope valkey MSC01-C key unlabeled at run 274 (401).
- TP (medium): util.c:1532. vsnprintf_async_signal_safe's switch on the conversion character lists d/i/u/x/p and s only, with no default.
- TP: valkey-cli.c:8456. latencyModePrint's chain on config.output handles STANDARD/CSV/RAW/JSON and not OUTPUT_QUOTED_JSON (defined at line 83, set by --quoted-json at line 2638), with no final else.
- TP (medium): valkey-cli.c:9668. bytesToHuman's size chain ends at < 1024^4, with no final else, so larger values write nothing.
- TP (medium): valkey-benchmark.c:719. The cluster error-reply chain handles MOVED/ASK and CLUSTERDOWN only, although the comment at lines 713-714 states other errors should exit.
- Medium FPs: t_hash.c:2212, t_zset.c:4193 (the object type restricts robj->encoding to the two encodings handled); t_list.c:334 (where is LIST_HEAD or LIST_TAIL); valkey-cli.c:8246 (the SCAN cursor reply is string or integer).
- No misfires. vset.c:2340 lists every bucket type with return false after the switch, so it is FP under the fallback clause.

Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision/recall claim is made here.
